scams.name: Fake Taxi Drivers at Ibiza Airport (IBZ)
scams.description: Ibiza has a documented 2025 problem with unauthorised drivers posing as licensed taxis. Community warnings alert travelers about an increasing number of individuals posing as taxi drivers, especially inside the terminal and in nearby pickup zones. The scam: a person in casual dress approaches arriving tourists, claims to be a licensed driver, and quotes a 'fixed price' of €60–€120 for rides that should cost €20–€35 on a legitimate meter. The vehicle often has no taxi licence number, no meter, and no printed receipt capability. Some drivers also take long routes to inflate already-fixed prices. Travelers confirm the legitimate rank is usually well-supplied: 'Never waited more than ten minutes in the cab line right outside.' Community reports from Naples and elsewhere document the same 'solicit inside the terminal' pattern across Mediterranean hubs — a Spain/Italy-wide airport-scam genre. For older travelers arriving at IBZ during peak season (May–October), the practical defence: (1) use ONLY the licensed yellow taxi rank immediately outside Arrivals — never engage with drivers inside the terminal or in nearby 'pickup zones'; (2) confirm the fare before boarding (€20–€25 to Ibiza Town, €25–€35 to San Antonio or Santa Eulalia, €15–€20 to Playa d'en Bossa); (3) insist on the meter and note the modo setting; (4) photograph the taxi licence number from the rear windscreen; (5) pre-book via Cabify if available (not all Ibiza routes are covered); (6) many Ibiza hotels offer fixed-price airport transfers — verify the rate against taxi-meter baseline before accepting.
scams.avoidance: Use ONLY the licensed yellow taxi rank immediately outside Arrivals at IBZ Confirm fare before boarding: €20–€25 Ibiza Town, €25–€35 San Antonio, €15–€20 Playa d'en Bossa Insist on the meter and note the modo setting Photograph the taxi licence number from the rear windscreen on entering Decline any driver who approaches inside the terminal — all are unauthorised
scams.location: Ibiza Airport (IBZ) arrivals hall and terminal approach, unauthorised 'taxi' vehicles without meters or licensing, pickup zones away from the official rank

scams.name: Nightclub 'Rep Ticket' & Promoter Commission Scam
scams.description: Ibiza's nightclub economy runs on promoter commissions — individuals called 'reps' or 'promoters' sell club tickets on the street and earn a percentage for each entry they bring in. The line between legitimate commission and scam is thin: genuine reps sell tickets at or near the door price with small markup (€5–€10); scam variants sell counterfeit wristbands, tickets to a different club than promised, or 'VIP packages' at 2–3x the door price with no actual benefit. Community reports warn that any transaction outside the club's official box office is risky; travelers consistently advise booking through the club's official website or resale platforms, never street reps. 2025 reports note that even 'legitimate' rep tickets are overpriced vs official channels: 'It's not a scam and the tickets are legit, it's just usually they charge a lot more than the clubs would directly.' For older travelers unlikely to club-hop but still curious about the Ibiza scene, the practical rule: (1) if you want to attend Pacha, Amnesia, Ushuaïa, Hï, or DC10, book tickets directly from the club's official website; (2) resale platforms (Xceed, Tixel, Ibiza Club News) are more reliable than street reps; (3) never buy wristbands from a street rep — counterfeit wristbands are rejected at the door; (4) 'VIP table' offers from reps are almost always scams — book direct via the club's VIP booking line; (5) a €80–€120 face-value ticket resold at €150–€200 by a rep is overpriced; walk away.
scams.avoidance: Book club tickets directly from the official website: pacha.com, amnesia.es, ushuaiaibiza.com, hiibiza.com, dc10ibiza.com Use resale platforms (Xceed, Tixel, Ibiza Club News) rather than street reps Never buy wristbands from a street rep — counterfeit wristbands rejected at door VIP tables booked only via the club's official VIP booking line If a face-value €80–€120 ticket is resold at €150+, walk away
scams.location: San Antonio 'West End' strip, Playa d'en Bossa club entrances, Ibiza Town Marina promoters, Rio Bar and other promoter hotspots

scams.name: Drink Spiking & Nightlife Theft in Ibiza Clubs
scams.description: Ibiza has documented 2025 reports of drink spiking and post-spiking theft targeting solo travellers and couples. One 2025 first-person account notes: 'I haven't heard anyone say spiking is a major concern, but you should always keep your drink attended.' The community view ranges from 'rare but real' to 'increasing 2025 concern.' A 2025 Ibiza victim wrote: 'A few months ago, I had the most terrifying experience of my life in Ibiza... I think the drink was spiked' — the victim lost consciousness and had valuables stolen. UK-wide community reports give the baseline: there are about 100–200 reports of spiking a week with very few successful prosecutions, and Ibiza's tourist-heavy nightlife concentration amplifies this. Community reports document the broader risk ecosystem. The scam variants: (1) open-drink spiking by a stranger to incapacitate for theft; (2) 'private villa' party invitations where the victim is separated from their group and robbed; (3) 'after-hours' invitations that lead to isolated locations. For older travellers unlikely to be in nightclub-scene target zones but still at ancillary risk (cocktail-bar encounters, 'private boat' tours), the practical defence: (1) NEVER leave a drink unattended — not even for 60 seconds; (2) order bottled drinks where possible and open them yourself; (3) travel with a trusted companion and set 'buddy check-in' rules for 2–3 AM and 5 AM; (4) decline all invitations to private villas or 'after-hours' parties from strangers; (5) if you feel unexpectedly disoriented, ask the bar staff for help IMMEDIATELY — Ibiza clubs have medical staff and can call ambulance services fast; (6) notify hotel staff and Policía Nacional Ibiza (+34 971 301 100) immediately if spiking suspected.
scams.avoidance: Never leave a drink unattended — not even for 60 seconds Order bottled drinks where possible and open them yourself Travel with a trusted companion; set buddy check-in rules for 2–3 AM and 5 AM Decline invitations to private villas or 'after-hours' parties from strangers If you feel disoriented, ask bar staff for help IMMEDIATELY; they have trained protocols
scams.location: San Antonio 'West End' bars, Playa d'en Bossa super-clubs, Ibiza Town nightlife, after-hours parties and 'private villa' events

scams.name: Mr Rental / Scooter & Rental Car Scams
scams.description: Ibiza's rental-transport economy has generated Spain's most-named 2025 scam-operator complaint. A community thread about a specific Ibiza rental operator, Mr Rental Ibiza, describes how travelers rented a scooter for one day at an operator with 4.6 stars on Google but repeated community complaints of damage-claim fraud, deposit retention, and fuel-policy overcharging. The fact that the operator maintains high Google ratings while generating consistent community complaints suggests systematic review manipulation. 2025 reports confirm Okmobility and Doyouspain operate at Ibiza Airport alongside Mr Rental: 'This company is a scam, preying on customers with unfair charges and then refusing to provide any support.' Other 2025 reports flag Ibiza alongside other Spanish rental hotspots. The scam patterns: (1) post-return damage claims with fabricated photos; (2) fuel-policy 'return empty' variants that overcharge for partial-tank returns; (3) deposit retention after scooter return citing 'late return' or 'cleaning fees'; (4) pressure to accept 'zero-excess' insurance at 3x the online rate. For older travellers considering Ibiza rental transport (car or scooter), the practical playbook: (1) AVOID Mr Rental Ibiza, Okmobility, Doyouspain, Goldcar, and Centauro — community-flagged repeat scammers; (2) book direct with Hertz, Europcar, or local Class Rent a Car (community-vetted) for better reliability; (3) at pickup, video a walk-around narrating visible marks; (4) photograph all sides, seats, mirrors, and tyres of scooters; (5) confirm fuel policy in writing before signing; (6) on return, video the returned vehicle and note the drop-off time; (7) dispute damage claims with your credit card within 48 hours; (8) for older travellers, consider licensed taxis or the L3 bus (Ibiza Town–Playa d'en Bossa) rather than scooter rental — Ibiza traffic is aggressive and many accidents involve tourist scooter drivers.
scams.avoidance: AVOID Mr Rental Ibiza, Okmobility, Doyouspain, Goldcar, Centauro — flagged operators Book direct with Hertz, Europcar, or Class Rent a Car (community-vetted) Video walk-around narrating visible marks at pickup before signing paperwork Photograph all sides, seats, mirrors, and tyres of scooters Dispute damage claims with credit card within 48 hours using photo/video evidence
scams.location: Ibiza Airport rental desks, Ibiza Town and San Antonio scooter rental shops, Playa d'en Bossa moped hire, 'Mr Rental Ibiza' specifically flagged

scams.name: O Beach / Ushuaïa Restaurant Minimum-Spend & Waiter Overcharge
scams.description: Ibiza's 'super-club' beach restaurants (O Beach, Ushuaïa, Nikki Beach) operate on a minimum-spend model that turns a lunch into a €200+ per-person experience. The scam variants: (1) minimum-spend enforcement that is not clearly disclosed at seating; (2) waiters who add €18+ glasses of wine to bills without ordering; (3) service charge of 15%+ added automatically; (4) pushy upsells for 'house champagne' at €80+ when requested 'a glass of wine.' One 2025 traveler wrote: 'We had a meal in the O Beach Restaurant and had to have a minimum spend of €100, which was easy because bottles of champagne and €15 waters drove the bill quickly.' Another 2025 report describes the specific waiter scam at Ushuaïa: 'We ordered two glasses of wine (€18 each) several times during the evening. A waitress tried at least three times to add extra glasses to the bill that were never ordered.' Community reports capture the 2025 auto-tip concern: 'Some restaurants are doing AUTOMATIC 15% tips so look on your receipt for it!' — these are pushing tips beyond the traditional Spanish no-tipping culture. Community reports include Ibiza cross-references for extreme resort-pricing. For older travellers curious about the Ibiza beach-club experience without the overcharge risk: (1) book a sunbed-only experience rather than a meal — most clubs offer €50–€80 sunbeds with minimum-spend waived or reduced; (2) if eating, request the minimum-spend contract in writing at seating; (3) check your bill line-by-line — waiters add items that were never ordered; (4) decline 'house champagne' upsells; order 'a glass of house wine' with the price stated; (5) photograph the menu and your order; (6) consider alternatives: S'Escalinata (Dalt Vila), Sa Capella (San Antonio), Cas Costas (San Rafael) for genuine Ibiza dining at honest prices; (7) for sunset without the beach-club premium, Café del Mar's terrace in San Antonio is €10–€15 per cocktail vs €25+ at O Beach.
scams.avoidance: Book sunbed-only experience (€50–€80) rather than a meal at O Beach, Ushuaïa, Nikki Beach Request minimum-spend contract in writing at seating if dining Check bill line-by-line; dispute items never ordered immediately Decline 'house champagne' upsells; order 'a glass of house wine' with stated price Alternative venues: S'Escalinata (Dalt Vila), Sa Capella (San Antonio), Cas Costas (San Rafael)
scams.location: O Beach Ibiza, Ushuaïa Beach Club, Nikki Beach, beach-club restaurants on Playa d'en Bossa and San Antonio bay

scams.name: Ibiza Villa Airbnb & Short-Term Rental Fraud
scams.description: Ibiza's villa-rental economy during the May–October season has produced Spain's most-documented accommodation-fraud pattern. Community reports warn of 'an incredible amount of scams' specifically targeting Ibiza villa rentals during peak season. The scam patterns: (1) listing at 30–50% below market rate for a luxury villa; (2) 'host' demands full payment via bank transfer or Bizum before arrival; (3) on arrival, the villa either doesn't exist, is already occupied, or is a lower-quality property than pictured; (4) 'host' disappears; (5) double-booking of the same villa to multiple guests on overlapping dates. The sophistication extends to private villa agencies. Community PSAs warn that some agency listings — even those with polished websites — are not legally licensed under Ibiza's short-term-rental registration system; guests arrive to find the villa's real owner has reported them as unauthorised occupants, triggering police involvement. Reports frame the broader 'Ibiza scam ecosystem' context that extends beyond just transport. For older travellers considering an Ibiza villa stay, the protective playbook: (1) book only through Airbnb, Booking.com, or VRBO with platform-verified payment and cancellation protection; (2) verify the property has an Ibiza Tourist Registration number (VT number — required for all licensed short-term rentals); (3) demand a video call with the villa visible before any deposit; (4) reverse-image-search villa photos on Google Images before paying; (5) refuse Bizum, Western Union, or cryptocurrency payment for any deposit; (6) for villa agencies, verify the company's Ibiza Council licensing through Consell de Eivissa (ibiza.travel); (7) if defrauded on arrival, file a denuncia at Policía Nacional Ibiza (+34 971 301 100) immediately.
scams.avoidance: Book only through Airbnb, Booking.com, or VRBO with platform-verified payment Verify VT tourist registration number — required for all licensed Ibiza short-term rentals Demand a video call with the villa visible before any deposit Reverse-image-search villa photos on Google Images before paying If defrauded on arrival, file denuncia at Policía Nacional Ibiza (+34 971 301 100) immediately
scams.location: Online — Airbnb villa listings for Ibiza season (May–October), private villa agency referrals, Booking.com listings with 'no-show' or 'changed location' scams
